answer: **Yes.** Although the passage relies almost entirely on sight, its visual details are precise and grounding. Georg sits on a spring Sunday morning in a first-floor room. The low, lightly built houses along the river differ "only in height and coloring." He leans his elbow on the desk and looks out at the river, the bridge, and the hills with their "faint green." The friend is pictured with a foreign-looking full beard and sallow, yellowish skin. These concrete, restrained observations anchor the more abstract reflections in a tangible setting and make the world feel real, even though sound, smell, taste, and touch are largely absent.
